sentences.text: Shri Kunal Samak, Advocate for the applicant.

Shri Apoorv Joshi, Govt. Advocate for the respondent/
 ORDER Learned counsel for the State submits that the victim has duly been informed about filing of the bail application.

This first application has been filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.492/2024, registered at Police Station - Dindayal Nagar, Ratlam,
District Ratlam(M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n), 376(3) of IPC and Sections 5(L)/6 and 5(J)(ii) of POCSO Act, 2012.
The applicant is in custody since 18.06.2025.
Heard the arguments.
Perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application, case diary and the relevant material on record.

Learned counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the applicant is falsely implicated NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24625 2 MCRC-37707-2025 in the alleged offence under the pressure of family members of the victim.
The applicant has not committed the alleged offence.
It is a case of teenage romance between two adolescents.

Learned counsel referring to the evidence of victim (PW-1), her father(PW-2) and her Prakash Maida vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164992522/
1 mother (PW-3) contends that the material prosecution witnesses did not support the prosecution and have exonerated the applicant of the alleged offence in their evidence before the trial Court.

sentences.text: Rather, they stated that the victim was major at the time of alleged incident.
There is no likelihood of tampering with the remaining evidence by the applicant for the reason that the material prosecution witnesses have been examined.
Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the young applicant and his family members.
Applicant is ready to cooperate in further trial.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
However, after going through the case diary, he fairly states that no criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.

According to the material available on case diary, applicant Prakash, aged around 20 years,
subjected the victim, aged around 15 years and 03 months, to penetrative sexual assault.
The material prosecution witnesses have already been examined and they have exonerated the applicant from the alleged offence.
The veracity of prosecution and the age of the victim will be determined after evidence in the trial.
As informed, the applicant is aged around 20 years.
He is labourer by profession.

He is still dependent on his family and survives on occasional NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:24625 3 MCRC-37707-2025 labour work.
Considering these aspects, there appears to be no possibility of fleeing from justice.

In absence of any criminal antecedent,
considering the socio-economic status of the applicant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with remaining evidence or influencing the remaining witnesses by the applicant.
There appears to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of the young applicant.
However, the observations, herein- above, are recorded for present application only.

Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the case, in the light of aforestated facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant-Prakash Maida shall be released on bail in connection with Crime, as mentioned in first paragraph of this order, upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/-(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) with one surety of the same amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, for compliance with the following conditions :
(For convenience of understanding by accused and surety, the conditions of bail are also reproduced in Hindi as under):-
(1) Applicant shall remain present on every date of hearing as may be directed by the concerned court; (1)         
      (2) Applicant shall not commit or get involved in any offence of similar nature; (2)
